transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Auric Head of ML), Tom Graves (Auric Platform Eng), Priya Kapoor (Auric Security)

Summary: Quick intake for Dedicated (reserved GPUs) - sizing, isolation, burst strategy and what falls back to Hosted; security gating items.

Topics: reserved GPU sizing; tenant isolation / node segregation; warm-pool and pre-warm strategies; VPC/on-prem options; KMS and audit logging; rollout timeline and pilot plan.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're on the call to go over your dedicated needs, try to size the reservation and understand isolation and burst patterns. can you kick off with a quick context?
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: yeah thanks maya. i'm lena, lead on the ml team. our use is two main workloads — interactive chat across our product and a background batch rerank pipeline. chat is latency sensitive, batch is throughput. goal is consistent 99th pct latency under 250 ms for chat, cost target to be below current on-prem spend.
[00:39] Tom Graves: i run platform, we already have k8s on EKS and use a private subnet for some infra. curious about VPC peering, ipsec, and whether we can get dedicated nodes that are logically isolated.
[00:56] Priya Kapoor: and i'm priya from security — SOC2 is required, also customer data residency in eu-west. we use customer-managed keys (KMS) and expect audit logs to integrate with our SIEM.
[01:12] Ravi Patel: great. quick question on workloads — when you say chat 99th at 250ms, is that end-to-end from client or from our inference endpoint?
[01:22] Lena Ortiz: from client, so network plus inference. the inference bucket should be ~100-120ms at 99th ideally.
[01:31] Maya Chen: okay that helps. we typically recommend reserved pools sized to steady-state plus a burst buffer; busy days hit 3x baseline for a couple hours. what does your traffic profile look like?
[01:42] Lena Ortiz: our p95 is pretty stable but we have weekly spikes. baseline concurrent requests about 60, peak 200 for 1-2 hours.
[01:52] Tom Graves: clarification — are those concurrent user sessions or calls? also, what model sizes?
[02:02] Lena Ortiz: sessions, roughly 1.5 calls per session. models — we're evaluating a 13B fine-tuned instruct model for chat, and a lighter 7B for rerank.

[05:00] Ravi Patel: (dialogue) okay so two model classes. for dedicated pools we usually recommend reserving enough GPU footprints to cover baseline concurrency on larger model and put smaller models on shared or pinned nodes. that gives you isolation but cheaper run for rerank in a mixed pool.
[05:24] Maya Chen: we also support pre-warm warm-pools — you can configure hotpool size to reduce cold start. question for you: how tolerant is the application to a fallback to our hosted tier during bursts?
[05:38] Lena Ortiz: acceptable for non-sensitive requests. but for PII or payments we need to keep inference in private/dedicated only.
[05:46] Priya Kapoor: that's key. any fallback must respect data residency and KMS boundaries — we can't send PII to hosted endpoints.
[05:55] Maya Chen: understood — policy-based routing possible: tag requests, route sensitive ones to Dedicated/reserved and non-sensitive can overflow to hosted. we'll include that in the proposal.

[12:10] Tom Graves: network questions — does the private deployment option allow direct VPC peering, or do you require an egress path? and what about latency between our VPC and the GPUs?
[12:26] Ravi Patel: for Redwood Private we can deploy into your VPC (VPC connectors) so compute lives in your network — lowers latency and meets your residency needs. for Dedicated (Redwood-managed) we support VPN or AWS PrivateLink depending on region; peering is available for some cloud partners. latency is usually single-digit ms for same-region peering.
[12:48] Tom Graves: good. what about IPs and tenant isolation — can we reserve nodes so no other tenant runs on the same host?
[12:56] Ravi Patel: yes, isolated tenancy is an option — dedicated instances/nodes for your account. additionally we can use node selectors to pin model variants to those nodes. note that fully isolated nodes reduce statistical multiplexing so cost goes up.

[18:30] Lena Ortiz: can you explain the burst policy? like, if we hit 200 concurrent, do you auto-scale on Dedicated or fallback to hosted? and how does warm-pool factoring work?
[18:44] Maya Chen: you can configure policies. option A: autoscale within Dedicated up to a reserved burst (if you bought burst credits) then fail or queue. Option B: overflow to hosted for eligible requests. warm-pool keeps pre-loaded KV caches and pre-warmed kernels to reduce token latency. we tune pre-warm size by model and typical sequence length.
[19:05] Ravi Patel: practical note — KV cache warmup time means first large context after a warm-pool restart will be slower. we sometimes recommend keeping a small hotpool of 1-2 nodes that are always live for low-latency tail.
[19:20] Priya Kapoor: how is data encrypted in transit and at rest? KMS integration? we need control of keys.
[19:28] Maya Chen: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and for Dedicated via a bring-your-key option in our enterprise plan. audit logs for inference requests, model versions, and admin access are exportable to your SIEM.

[26:05] Ravi Patel: on sizing math — if 13B model on A100-like GPU gives you X tokens/sec (i'll attach our baseline), for your p95 targets, we estimate needing 4-6 GPUs for steady-state and 10-12 for peak if you want no fallback. with a warm-pool of 2 nodes we get much better 99th pct.
[26:29] Lena Ortiz: hmm 10-12 is more than we planned. our budget may not allow full headroom. can we do a hybrid — reserved for baseline plus overflow to hosted for non-PII?
[26:42] Maya Chen: absolutely, that's a common pattern. we'll propose a hybrid with policy rules and an audit trail for what went to hosted vs dedicated.

[33:40] Tom Graves: operationally, who manages kernel selection and quantization? do we need to test our fine-tuned model with you?
[33:50] Ravi Patel: Redwood handles kernel selection in the runtime; for best results we do a model onboarding where we run a short bench using your artifact. we can also recommend quantization profiles that keep quality within acceptable regs. we'll need your model checkpoint and a sample prompt set for eval.
[34:12] Lena Ortiz: we can't upload full checkpoints to hosted. what's the secure onboarding path?
[34:18] Maya Chen: for private/on-prem we can do ingestion inside your VPC or air-gapped package. for dedicated we provide encrypted transfer and you can pre-supply via secure S3 with restricted access and lifetime tokens.

[40:20] Priya Kapoor: audit perspective — we need immutable logs for model requests, admin actions, and key rotations. retention policy is 12 months. can that be configured?
[40:32] Maya Chen: yes configurable retention windows and integration points for log shipping. longer retention is an add-on.
[40:40] Tom Graves: rollout timeline — what's a pilot look like? two weeks of bench + one small production lane?
[40:48] Ravi Patel: typical pilot: 2 week onboarding + 1 week of soak with canary routes. we instrument with per-route dashboards and tracing hooks so you can see latency, token costs, and error rates.

[45:00] Maya Chen: ok wrap up — we will: size two proposals (hybrid with overflow + full dedicated with higher headroom), include a break-down of cost by token and reserved GPU vs burst, and outline security integrations.
[45:15] Lena Ortiz: good. please include a sample SLA for the Dedicated pool and what fallback looks like.
[45:22] Priya Kapoor: and include SOC2 artefacts and KMS architecture notes.
[45:30] Maya Chen: noted. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and pricing by Friday.
[45:40] Tom Graves: thanks all, bye.
[45:50] (call ends)
